project.clientName: Dr Alexandra Featherstone-Montgomery & Mr Christopher Featherstone-Montgomery
project.projectDescription: New two-storey architectural home with basement cellar, lap pool and detached studio
project.siteAddress: Lot 212, 48 Woodcutters Ridge Road, Aldgate SA 5154 (Adelaide Hills Face Zone)
project.deliveryModel: Design & Build (fixed-price contract to follow pre-construction)
project.drawingBasis: Concept Set C-04 Rev B, issued 31 Oct 2026

intentions.label: Sit low
intentions.text: Settle the home into the Hills Face landscape with a restrained palette.

intentions.label: Bring in light
intentions.text: Prioritise northern light, acoustic calm and indoor–outdoor flow.

intentions.label: Build to last
intentions.text: Durable, low-maintenance materials and bushfire-ready detailing.

summaryParas: A new two-storey family home on a sloping Adelaide Hills Face Zone allotment, designed to sit low in the landscape with a restrained, durable material palette and strong indoor–outdoor connection to the north. The clients value natural light, acoustic calm and low ongoing maintenance.
This brief records the direction confirmed through concept and early pre-construction so detailed design and documentation can proceed from a single shared source.
scopeIn: New two-storey dwelling with partial basement (cellar + store) and integrated double garage.
Lap pool with travertine-look surround and equipment enclosure.
Detached studio / home office to the rear, serviced for future use.
Full landscape and driveway within the approved building envelope.
scopeOut: Solar battery system — priced separately as an option.
Furniture, loose fittings and window furnishings beyond the fixed scope.
Any works outside the approved Hills Face Zone building envelope.

preferenceGroups.name: External
items: Combination of through-coloured render and vertical spotted-gum cladding, low-sheen dark metal roof.
Bushfire-compliant (BAL-rated) windows and doors; the final BAL rating is to be confirmed with the energy/bushfire assessor.

preferenceGroups.name: Internal
items: Large-format porcelain to entry and wet areas; engineered timber to living and bedrooms.
Honed stone benchtops; integrated joinery with minimal hardware.

assumptions: Geotechnical and bushfire assessments to be completed in pre-construction and may adjust footings and envelope detailing.
Allowances shown anywhere in supporting documents are indicative only and are superseded by the developed cost plan.

questions.action: Confirm basement extent against the developed cost plan.
Confirm pool position and its interface with the Hills Face Zone envelope.
Confirm the structural and bushfire certification pathway before working drawings.

nextStepsParas: Blue Leaf will complete the developed design and specification with the consultant team, confirm engineering and certification, and issue a developed cost plan and tender package ahead of the fixed-price building contract.

actions.action: Provide the outstanding BAL (bushfire) assessment — it governs cladding, glazing and decking selections.
Coordinate basement waterproofing and drainage with the structural and civil packages (ST-01).
Confirm the pool position against the Hills Face Zone building envelope (PL-01).
Confirm the certification pathway (private certifier vs council) before working drawings.
Reconcile the BAL rating consistently across windows, cladding and decking before finalising selections.

purposeParas: Issued to the design team to progress developed documentation for a new two-storey home with basement, pool and studio on a Hills Face Zone allotment. Latest basis: Concept Set C-04 Rev B. Confirmed client requirements and indicative preferences are separated below; the coordination schedule lists each item's status and the action required.
confirmedReqs: Two-storey dwelling with partial basement and integrated double garage, per Concept Set C-04 Rev B.
North-facing primary living with deep eaves; home to sit below the ridgeline sightline.
BAL-rated external envelope; final rating from the bushfire assessment to govern detailing.
clientPrefs: Through-coloured render with spotted-gum cladding accents; dark low-sheen metal roof.
Large-format porcelain to wet areas; engineered timber elsewhere; honed stone benchtops.
Lap pool with travertine-look surround; studio serviced for future fit-out.

approachParas: A calm, confident new home built on a consistent material language — a restrained masonry-and-metal exterior, warm honest interiors and a small number of considered feature elements. This presentation groups the current selections for easy review; the technical selection register and the architectural drawings remain the definitive source.
Items shown here reflect the direction developed to date. Where an item is still being reviewed it is marked accordingly, and the decisions list at the end sets out what remains to be confirmed.
